Exit code 1
# Absys

**Evidence class: reconstructed.** No Absys implementation survives. The
system used is the reconstruction in https://github.com/chrishayuk/absys,
built from Foster (1968), Foster and Elcock (1969), Elcock (1982) and
Elcock (1990). Every rule it follows, and the evidence for each, is in its
`docs/decisions.md`.

## Pinning

The commit used is fixed when the specification is frozen. It is
`efd5203` (`PINS.md`): `7bb61e6` with one defect of the printer fixed.
Printing a list that contains itself (`x = [x]`, P01c) overflowed the
stack after the computation had finished. Only the printer changed, and
every example and research text prints byte for byte as at `7bb61e6`
(160 runs), which is kept as the behavioural reference. The defect is
recorded in the reconstruction's `docs/decisions.md`. Any later change to the
reconstruction, for whatever reason, makes a new configuration, reported
separately beside the pinned one. Mechanisms added after the freeze are
never counted as native in the pinned configuration.

## Decisions taken while the precursor experiments ran

The reconstruction was built while the experiments E01–E09 ran. P01–P08
come from those experiments. These rules of the machine were set or changed
because of them:

| rule in `docs/decisions.md` | what it decides | prompted by |
|---|---|---|
| 10 | a primitive relation returns for each of its variables bound, to the head of the list | Elcock 1982's printed list (E06), the precursor of P02 |
| 15 | an applied body takes the place of its literal | setdiff under first-in first-out selection (E02), the precursor of P06d |
| 18, 19 | a `not` or `set` that cannot yet be decided waits and is run again | permuting the student and setdiff texts (E02, E03), the precursors of P06 and P08 |
| 6 | an application of an identifier with no value waits for it, and outside a lambda every identifier is shared by the whole text | E90 p. 10 for the waiting; the sharing across the whole text was made general when permuting E03, the precursor of P08 |

Results on P02, P06 and P08 should be read with this in mind. Rules 10 and
15 rest on readings of the sources that the experiments helped to choose;
rules 6, 18 and 19 are partly decisions where the sources are silent.

## Configurations

| configuration | what it is | class |
|---|---|---|
| **absys** | the reconstruction's defaults | reconstructed |
| absys-depth-first | `--search depth-first`: the backtracking reading of Elcock (1982) | reconstructed, alternative reading |
| absys-wake-back | `--wake back`: returned relations appended, as the word of Elcock (1982) says | reconstructed, alternative reading |

## The core

The machine as `docs/decisions.md` describes it, in the pinned commit:
equality as a process, with suspension of equations between unknowns;
`lambda` procedures applied in any direction; `or`, distributed into
derivations; `not` and `set`; `key`; arithmetic as relations over
integers, taken up when two of three values are known; `tout`; and the
incremental acceptance of assertions. Nothing else exists to be imported,
so every Absys configuration has no external mechanisms.

## Notation

Absys is known in three notations: Absys 1 (1969), the 1982 paper's, and
the 1990 retrospective's. Absys 1 has arithmetic, and the 1990 notation has
`not` and `set`. The notation for each problem is fixed by a rule, not
chosen: the **earliest** notation that has every construct the problem
needs. A problem that needs constructs found in no single notation is
recorded as such, with the notation used.

**No comparisons.** The pinned reconstruction has +, −, · and ÷ as
relations, and no <, ≤, > or ≥, as calibration found. Three claims are kept
apart:

| claim | status |
|---|---|
| the pinned reconstruction has no comparison operators | established |
| the notations recovered from the sources show none | supported by the sources examined: Foster (1968), the extracts of Foster and Elcock (1969), Elcock (1982) and Elcock (1990) |
| historical Absys never had comparisons | **not established**. The full description of Absys-4 (Elcock and Gray, 1988) and the program itself have not been seen |

Expressibility is recorded per **sub-problem**, not per problem family. A
sub-problem that needs a comparison cannot be transcribed: P05's x > 1,
P09c's n > 5, P10d's x > 1, P11's x ≥ 2, P12's n > 0, P13a–d's range, and
P15d. The other sub-problems of the same problem are recorded on their
own. The rule for every system then applies (`SPECIFICATION.md`,
expressibility):

- where a reformulation without the comparison keeps the meaning on every
  input the problem and its variants use (replacing n > 0 by an enumeration
  of the finitely many values used, for instance), it is the program of
  record, *expressible with reformulation*;
- where it does not (calibration's range, with m > n replaced by
  m = n + 1 and m ≤ n dropped, which leaves an endless derivation), the
  sub-problem is *not expressible*, and the reformulation is a named
  variant.

**Output.** The baseline prints at most 32 elements of a list and 24
derivations. The instrumented commit `5450449` (branch `measure`) adds
`--full`, which prints both in full, so `observe()` can read every answer.
With no occur check, a computation can end with a cyclic value (P01c), so
`--full` detects a list cell met again while it is being printed, and
prints `↻` for "the enclosing list again": X = [1|X] prints `[1|↻]`,
X = [X] prints `[↻]`. Tests cover cyclic tails and heads, cycles through
two variables, long and partly known lists, and many derivations.
Against the baseline, its default output is identical in all 140 runs, and
`--full` output is identical in the 132 runs the baseline did not cut
short.

**A fault, found and fixed.** At `7bb61e6` the default printer overflowed
the stack on a cycle through a list's elements, X = [X]: the computation
finished, and printing its answer crashed. It was fixed on `main` as
`efd5203`, the pinned commit, which prints `[↻]` in every mode. The fault
is kept on record, in the reconstruction's `docs/decisions.md` and in
`PINS.md`. No result is taken from `7bb61e6`.

## Units

- **Step:** one step of the machine, as its `--steps` budget counts them:
  one equation or one literal elaborated in one derivation.
- **Alternative:** one derivation. All are live at once under **absys**.
  Under **absys-depth-first**, all are held too, but only the first is
  elaborated until it hibernates or fails, so the count is of derivations
  held, of which one is live.
  A derivation is not equated with a Prolog choicepoint, or with any
  other system's unit. Comparable counts come only from quantities a
  problem defines.
- **Store:** a vector, from `--measure` on the instrumented commit
  `f1a63aa` (branch `measure`; `5450449` adds `--full` and changes nothing
  measured). For each assertion it gives the value at
  the end and the peak, sampled after every step, so the peak is exact at
  the granularity of steps:

  | quantity | what it counts |
  |---|---|
  | derivations | live derivations of the top-level computation |
  | sub_derivations | derivations inside `not` and `set` computations |
  | variables | variables created, in every derivation. Derivations only gain variables, so for one derivation this is cumulative; it falls only when a derivation fails. It is listed, but it is not retained store in the sense the others are |
  | bindings | variables with a value |
  | susp_equations | suspended equations between two uninstantiated variables |
  | susp_applications | applications waiting for a definition or their key |
  | susp_relations | arithmetic and `tout` relations waiting for values |
  | susp_negations | `not` and `set` waiting to be decided or tried again |
  | pending | equations, literals and alternatives queued, not yet taken up |
  | term_nodes | nodes of bound values, counted in every derivation that holds them, without regard to sharing |

  term_nodes is a logical size, not memory. Derivations share structure,
  so the memory held is smaller.

The state is also sampled right after an assertion is added and before the
first step, so a peak at a stage boundary is not missed.

The instrumented commit changes nothing the machine computes on the texts
tested. That is observational equivalence over that corpus, not a proof
for every workload. With
`--measure` off and on, its output was identical to the baseline's, byte
for byte: 20 texts in 7 output modes (140 runs), full traces included,
and the JSON of all 20. This was checked against `7bb61e6`, and again
after the branch was rebased onto `efd5203`, with the same result; `--full`
output also matched wherever the baseline cut nothing short (132 runs). Measuring is slow, because the
whole state is read after every step. Step counts are unaffected; only
time is. Results report the baseline commit for behaviour and the
instrumented commit for store.

## The same computation

The reconstruction is incremental. Every stage is received into the same
session, with no reposing.

## Prior work, not results

The absys repository's experiments E01–E09 ran versions of P01–P08 before
this specification existed. They will be written again from the problem
files after the freeze.

76	qualification shows its output identical to the baseline `absys`'s on
77	every test (QUESTIONS, A2). `system_build.commit` is `5450449…`, read from
78	`/opt/src/COMMITS`, and `instrumented: true`.
79	
80	Two more environment variables: `HARNESS_EXACT_PEAK=1` makes storage
81	runs take the peak after every step (section 4), for small-scale
82	validation; `HARNESS_RUN_LABEL`, if set, is copied verbatim into the
83	record's `notes`. Absys has no version option,
84	so `version_output` is `null`.
85	
86	## 3. The program contract
87	
88	A program author cannot run the program before its results are taken, so
89	everything below is exact. Only `check` may be used before the program is
90	fixed.
91	
92	### 3.1 The file
93	
94	One file, UTF-8. **Its extension fixes the notation**, as the system's own
95	rule does (`src/session.rs`, `notation_for`): `.ab1` is the 1969 notation
96	(Absys 1, with arithmetic), `.ab2` the 1982 notation, anything else (use
97	`.abs`) the 1990 notation. Lines beginning with `%` are comments in all
98	three; the harness's markers are comments, so they are not tokens.
99	
100	The file is divided by marker lines (each on its own line; leading spaces
101	allowed; exact patterns):
102	
103	| marker | pattern | meaning |
104	|---|---|---|
105	| `% STAGE k` | `^\s*%\s*STAGE\s+(\d+)\s*$` | the text of stage *k* starts here |
106	| `% PART name` | `^\s*%\s*PART\s+(\S+)\s*$` | the text of the part *name* starts here (3.5); a program has STAGE sections or PART sections, not both |
107	| `% SPAWN c` | `^\s*%\s*SPAWN\s+(\S+)\s*$` | inside a stage's section: the text of the spawned computation *c* starts here (3.6) |
108	| `% PARAMETERS n order …` | `^\s*%\s*PARAMETERS\b(.*)$` | in the prelude: the instance parameters the program wants (3.4) |
109	| `% CONSTANTS BEGIN` / `% CONSTANTS END` | a comment line containing the words | the constants block (3.9), in the prelude: a table the harness reads, never given to the system |
110	
111	Everything before the first STAGE or PART marker is the **prelude**: the
112	definitions of the problem's relations and the constants block. A section
113	runs to the next STAGE or PART marker (a SPAWN subsection to the next
114	SPAWN, STAGE or PART marker). Marker lines are given to the system with
115	the section they begin; they are comments.
116	
117	### 3.2 How a stage is given to the system
118	
119	**Behaviour runs** start one `absys-measure repl` process and keep it for
120	the whole run: every stage is received into the same session, as the
121	systems file says ("The same computation"). The harness writes to its
122	standard input, in this order:
123	
124	1. at stage 1: one assertion per declared parameter (3.4), then the
125	   prelude's lines (without the constants block), then stage 1's section;
126	2. at stage *k*: stage *k*'s section, as the file has it but with each
127	   constant's name replaced by its value (3.9), line by line, **only when
128	   stage *k* is posed**. No line of a later section is
129	   ever written before its stage (no anticipation), and the program is
130	   never told how many stages follow.
131	
132	After each section, and after each piece of 1 (the parameters, the
133	prelude), the harness writes a line `.help`. The repl's reply to it is a
134	fixed text, which tells the harness that the system has finished with
135	everything before it (QUESTIONS, A3). The repl takes each line in turn and
136	does everything that can be done before it reads the next (each
137	assertion is elaborated until every derivation hibernates or fails, or the
138	budget runs out).
139	
140	**The repl reads a text line by line**, and that is the one constraint it
141	puts on layout (`src/main.rs`, `repl`). After each line it parses what it
142	has read since the last complete assertion:
143	
144	- if that parses, it is accepted at once, as one or more assertions;
145	- if it fails to parse only because it ends too soon, the repl reads on;
146	- otherwise it reports `error at L:C: message` and drops it.
147	
148	So, **a program must keep these rules**, which `check` enforces:
149	
150	1. **An assertion that spans several lines must not be complete at the
151	   end of any of its lines but the last.** End a line with `or`, `,`,
152	   an open `{` or `[`, or `=`, never at a point where the assertion could
153	   end. `colour = lambda C {C = 'red'} or` followed by `{C = 'green'}` is
154	   right; `colour = lambda C {C = 'red'}` followed by a line
155	   `or {C = 'green'}` is two assertions to the repl, the second a syntax
156	   error.
157	2. **Every section ends with a complete assertion.** Otherwise the repl
158	   reads the harness's `.help` as the assertion's continuation and
159	   reports a syntax error (``error at L:1: `.` is not in the notation``),
160	   which the harness records as the stage's error.
161	3. **No line, outside an unfinished assertion, may begin with `?` or
162	   `.`.** The repl takes such a line as a command (`.quit` ends it).
163	
164	**Cost and storage runs** cannot use the repl, which reports no step
165	count and no store: the system reports them only for a whole text,
166	`absys-measure FILE --measure`. So each stage *k* is one new process on a
167	text the harness writes: the parameters' assertions, the prelude and the
168	sections of stages 1 to *k*, in order, exactly as above. Its session takes
169	the assertions one at a time, as the repl's does, and the qualification
170	shows that its states and step counts at every stage are those of the
171	incremental behaviour run. These records show every stage after the first
172	as `reposed` (`reason: "configuration"`), with the steps of stages 1 to
173	*k*−1 as restart cost, which the behaviour run does not pay (QUESTIONS,
174	A4).
175	
176	### 3.3 What the program writes in a stage's section
177	
178	The stage's information, as Absys assertions: equations, applications,
179	`or`, `not`, `set`, `tout`, procedure definitions (a stage may define a
180	procedure, P08 for instance). A replacing or retracting stage (P10, P15d)
181	is whatever assertions the program uses to carry it out; the harness
182	gives the section as written, every one of them, on every replay.
183	
184	**Identifiers.** As the reconstruction decides (`docs/decisions.md`, rule
185	6): outside any lambda every identifier is shared by the whole text, so a
186	name given a value in the prelude, the constants block or an earlier
187	stage is the same variable in every later stage. In the 1990 notation,
188	inside a lambda an identifier with a capital that the lambda does not
189	bind is local, and one with a small letter is shared; in the 1969
190	notation a primed name is local; in the 1982 notation, a name the body
191	uses but never applies, and the lambda does not bind, is local. So a
192	constant used inside a lambda must be written with a small letter (1990)
193	or not be primed (1969).
194	
195	**Name each unknown as `stages.json` names it** (`x`, `total`, …), where
196	the notation allows it: `observe()` asks the system for each unknown by
197	that name (3.8). Every identifier of the text that is not a procedure is
198	printed in every derivation, so the parameters' names appear in the
199	answers too. The constants' names do not: the system never sees them
200	(3.9).
201	
202	### 3.4 Instance parameters
203	
204	A program that needs an instance's parameters (n, an order, a spawn
205	order, the answer mode) names them on one line of the prelude:
206	
207	    % PARAMETERS n order
208	
209	For each name, in that order, the harness gives the system, at stage 1,
210	before the prelude, one assertion `NAME = VALUE`, in the program's
211	notation:
212	
213	| value | 1990 (`.abs`) | 1969 (`.ab1`) | 1982 (`.ab2`) |
214	|---|---|---|---|
215	| `"n": 1000` | `n = 1000` | `n = 1000` | `n = 1000` |
216	| `"order": ["R2", "R1", "R3"]` | `order = ['R2', 'R1', 'R3']` | `order = ['R2';'R1';'R3']` | `order = ['R2','R1','R3']` |
217	| `"answers": "all"` | `answers = 'all'` | `answers = 'all'` | `answers = 'all'` |
218	| `"spawn_order": ["A", "B"]` | `spawn_order = ['A', 'B']` | `spawn_order = ['A';'B']` | `spawn_order = ['A','B']` |
219	
220	The names are `n`, `order`, `answers`, `cap` and `spawn_order`, and only
221	those the instance has (`stages.json`). A program that declares none gets
222	none. The record lists what was passed (`posed.instance_parameters_passed`).
223	The harness never passes a constant of a problem.
224	
225	The answer mode needs nothing from the program: the harness's cap does it
226	(3.7). The spawn order needs nothing either (3.6).
227	
228	### 3.5 Arrival orders of written relations: PART sections (P02b, P07a)
229	
230	Where an instance's `order` names the stage's relations (`P02b.R2R1R3`:
231	R2, then R1, then R3; `P07a.312`: the third relation written, then the
232	first, then the second), a program may give each relation as a part,
233	named as the order names it:
234	
235	    % PART R1
236	    ...
237	    % PART R2
238	    ...
239	
240	At stage *k* the harness gives part `order[k-1]`. A program for the
241	instance in the written order (`P07a`, order `["1","2","3"]`) is the same
242	program. Orders that do not name stages (P16's `ascending`, …) are passed
243	only as the parameter `order` (3.4), and the program must use it itself.
244	
245	### 3.6 Spawned computations (P09a, P09b, P16b)
246	
247	A stage that spawns computations has, in its section, one SPAWN
248	subsection per computation, named as `stages.json` names them:
249	
250	    % STAGE 1
251	    % SPAWN A
252	    ...
253	    % SPAWN B
254	    ...
255	
256	Text in the section before the first SPAWN is given first. Then, for each
257	computation in the instance's `spawn_order` (or the order of the stage's
258	`spawns`), the harness gives its subsection, waits until the system has
259	done everything it can (every derivation hibernates or fails, or the
260	budget runs out), reads that computation's answers and state, and then
261	gives the next (`side_by_side: false`).
262	
263	**Absys has no separate computations**: one session holds one
264	computation, whose derivations every assertion is added to. A spawned
265	computation's text is accepted into that one computation, conjoined with
266	everything already there, and so it shares every unknown with the others
267	(QUESTIONS, A5). P16b's contributors are therefore spawned, not posed by
268	the fallback. Whether P09a ("not conjoined") is expressible in Absys is
269	for the program author and the classifiers; the harness does nothing to
270	separate them.
271	
272	### 3.7 Answers: the system's standard mechanism
273	
274	Absys reports a computation as its **derivations**, every one at once,
275	each with its bindings, the processes it suspends and its outputs, by
276	printing its state. That is the standard mechanism, and the program needs
277	nothing to use it. `answers(cap)` is the first `cap` derivations of the
278	state the system prints at the end of the stage (the repl's `?`), each
279	derivation's block verbatim, from its line `  derivation #N (…)` to the
280	next. Under `--full` every derivation is printed.
281	
282	| ended_by | when |
283	|---|---|
284	| `exhausted` | the system printed at most `cap` derivations (none, when no derivation survives) |
285	| `cap` | it printed more than `cap`; the rest are in `observe.raw` |
286	| `budget` | its state reports derivations still elaborating when the budget ran out |
287	| `error` | the system reported an error for the stage's text |
288	| `timeout` | the safety limit stopped the attempt |
289	
290	Absys elaborates every derivation before it reports any, so there is no
291	request for "more answers": a stage never ends *alternatives pending*
292	(QUESTIONS, A8). In cost mode each answer's `steps_at` is the stage's
293	steps, when the mechanism gave every answer at once.
294	
295	### 3.8 What `observe()` and `print()` read
296	
297	At the end of each stage (and for each spawned computation, after its
298	section) the harness writes the repl's own commands:
299	
300	- `?`: the state, every derivation with its status (`hibernating` or
301	  `still elaborating`), its outputs, its procedures, every identifier's
302	  value (with `(suspended: …)` where only suspended equations constrain
303	  it), its suspended processes, and what is still to do. This is
304	  `print`, and the start of `observe.raw`;
305	- `? NAME`, for each unknown of the sub-problem in `stages.json` written
306	  as a plain identifier: the system's value of NAME in each derivation
307	  (`#3: x = 2`), or `NAME does not occur`. These are `observe.bindings`,
308	  by unknown, verbatim, and follow in `observe.raw`.
309	
310	Both read and change nothing. In cost and storage runs, `print` and
311	`observe.raw` are the state `absys FILE` prints at the end of the text of
312	stages 1 to *k* (with `--each` in a stage that spawns, the state after
313	each assertion, from which each computation's is read).
314	
315	### 3.9 The constants block
316	
317	Every constant of every stage is in **one block in the prelude**, between
318	a comment line containing `CONSTANTS BEGIN` and one containing
319	`CONSTANTS END`. The block is a **table, never given to the system**: one
320	constant per line, `NAME = VALUE`, the value on that line (comment lines
321	and blank lines are allowed; a `%` ends the value):
322	
323	    % CONSTANTS BEGIN
324	    c1 = 41
325	    c2 = 'red'
326	    facts = [[1, 'a'], [2, 'b']]
327	    % CONSTANTS END
328	
329	The program's text refers to the constants by name (`pr = [c1, d]`).
330	**When the harness gives a section to the system, it replaces each name
331	of the table, in that section's text, by its value**, so that what the
332	system receives is `pr = [41, d]`. A constant therefore reaches the system
333	only with the section that uses it: a constant of stage 3 is not in the
334	system, as information or as a name, before stage 3 is posed (no
335	anticipation, `PROTOCOL.md`, "Writing a program", rule 5). A name used in
336	the prelude (in a definition) is given with the prelude, at stage 1.
337	
338	What is replaced, exactly: an identifier (the system's: a letter or `_`,
339	then letters, digits and `_`, and, after a small letter, `-` between
340	letters, as in `math-course`) equal to a name of the table. Nothing is
341	replaced inside a quoted constant (`'…'`, `"…"`), inside a comment, or in
342	a name written with a prime (1969: a new local name). The value is put in
343	as written in the table, with no change. So:
344	
345	- name constants with identifiers that the program uses for nothing else;
346	- a constant used inside a lambda is replaced like any other (the value,
347	  not the name, reaches the system, so the scoping rules of 3.3 do not
348	  arise).
349	
350	The verifier replaces only the lines between the markers. The harness
351	records `constants.how: "block"` when the markers are present, else
352	`"none"`. `check` parses each section after the replacement, as the
353	system will receive it, and reports a line of the block that is not
354	`NAME = VALUE`. Absys reads no input, so there is no `input` form.
355	
356	### 3.10 Effects (P11): emit
357	
358	The harness's `emit(m)` is written, in Absys,
359	
360	    tout("emit", M)
361	
362	with the term to emit as its second argument. `tout` is the system's own
363	output assertion (Elcock 1990, note 11): it waits until its term has no
364	uninstantiated variable, and then performs one output, `emit = VALUE`, in
365	the derivation it is in. In P11 runs the harness switches the system's
366	trace on (`.trace`, or `--trace`), and every `output` event of the trace
367	whose text begins `emit = ` becomes one entry of the log, `entry` being
368	the rest of it, the system's rendering of the term (`'red'`, `[1,2]`), in
369	the order the trace shows them. An output performed in a derivation that
370	later fails stays in the log: nothing the system does removes an entry.
371	Entries made while a reposed run replays an earlier stage carry
372	`during_replay_of`. Behaviour runs write to
373	`OUTDIR/<instance>.effects.jsonl`; the separate run that measures a
374	restart cost, and every cost and storage run, write to
375	`OUTDIR/<instance>.effects-observation.jsonl`. Neither is ever reset.
376	
377	**Commit stages** (P11c stage 3, P11d stage 2): Absys keeps every
378	derivation live and selects none. The section may be empty (comments
379	only). `answers(1)` reports the first derivation printed, as for any
380	any-one query; no commitment is recorded, and none is replayed when a
381	later stage is reposed (QUESTIONS, A6).
382	
383	### 3.11 Provenance
384	
385	At the top of the file, in comments, the lines `% AUTHOR: …`,
386	`% PRECURSOR-SEEN: yes|no` (whether its author had seen the E01–E09
387	programs) and `% IDIOM: …` (the source of each idiom). `check` warns if
388	there is no `AUTHOR` line.
389	
390	### 3.12 H tokens
391	
392	`METRICS.md`, class H: the harness's own calls as they appear in a
393	program. In an Absys program they are:
394	
395	| construct | H tokens |
396	|---|---|
397	| the emit stub's binding, `tout("emit", T)` | `tout`, `(`, `"emit"`, `,` and `)`; the term `T` is classed on its own (rule 10) |
398	
399	Nothing else in a program is H. The markers are comments; the parameter
400	assertions are written by the harness, not the program; answers are
401	collected from what the system prints by itself, with no call in the
402	program, so there is no output adapter. A program's uses of a parameter's
403	name (`n`), its constants block and its definitions are classed by the
404	rules of `METRICS.md`.
405	
406	### 3.13 A complete minimal example
407	
408	A made-up problem, not one of P01–P16 (`qualification/stages-qualification.json`, X10):
409	
410	> **X10a.** `pair(A, B, P)` holds when P is the list `[A, B]`.
411	> Stage 1: `pair(a, b, pr)`. Stage 2: `pr = [⟨k⟩, d]`. Stage 3: `d = ⟨atom⟩`.
412	> Unknowns a, b, pr, d. Constants: ⟨k⟩ = 41, ⟨atom⟩ = `'red'`.
413	
414	The program, `qualification/programs/x10-pair.abs`:
415	
416	```
417	% AUTHOR: harness-absys (an agent), for the harness's qualification. MADE UP: not a problem program.
418	% PRECURSOR-SEEN: no. IDIOM: a lambda procedure, as in Elcock 1990 p. 8.
419	% CONSTANTS BEGIN
420	c1 = 41
421	c2 = 'red'
422	% CONSTANTS END
423	pair = lambda A, B, P {P = [A, B]}
424	% STAGE 1
425	pair(a, b, pr)
426	% STAGE 2
427	pr = [c1, d]
428	% STAGE 3
429	d = c2
430	```
431	
432	What the system receives, in one session, and what the harness collects
433	(from the qualification's behaviour record):
434	
435	| stage | written to the repl | `answers(20)`: the one derivation | state |
436	|---|---|---|---|
437	| 1 | the prelude without the block (lines 1, 2 and 7), `.help`, `% STAGE 1` and `pair(a, b, pr)`, `.help`, then `?` and `? a`, `? b`, `? pr`, `? d` | `a  uninstantiated`, `b  uninstantiated`, `pr = [a,b]` | finished |
438	| 2 | `% STAGE 2`, `pr = [41, d]`, `.help`, `?`, … | `a = 41`, `b = d   (suspended: b = d)`, `pr = [41,b]`, `suspended   b = d` | suspended |
439	| 3 | `% STAGE 3`, `d = 'red'`, `.help`, `?`, … | `a = 41`, `b = 'red'`, `pr = [41,'red']`, `d = 'red'` | finished |
440	
441	41 is not in the system before stage 2, nor `'red'` before stage 3.
442	
443	Its H tokens: none. Snippets for the other forms are in
444	`qualification/programs/`: SPAWN (`x17-spawn.abs`), PART with a parameter
445	(`x19-parts.abs`), emit (`x18-emit.abs`), the 1969 notation
446	(`x20-arith.ab1`).
447	
448	## 4. Modes
449	
450	| mode | process | what is of record |
451	|---|---|---|
452	| behaviour | one `absys-measure repl --full` for the run (a new one only to repose) | answers, `observe`, `print`, execution state, the effects log. No step count: the repl reports none |
453	| cost | per stage, `absys-measure FILE --measure --peak-every 0 --full` on stages 1..k; `--trace` too where the budget is 10⁶ | `steps.stage` (the steps of stage k's assertions: the incremental cost), `steps.restated` (all of the run), `restart_cost` (stages 1..k−1, in-run), `to_end`, `repeated_work` |
454	| storage | the same command with `--peak-every 1000` (`1` under `HARNESS_EXACT_PEAK=1`), and `--trace` only in P11 | the store vector, `alternatives.peak` (derivations, exact), the state's suspended processes |
455	
456	- **Steps** are the system's (one step of the machine, as `--steps`
457	  counts them), read only from `--measure`'s table, the systems file's
458	  qualified measurement. Sampling the store adds time, not steps
459	  (systems file). Cost and storage records both keep what `--measure`
460	  gave; the figure of record is the mode's. Behaviour records have
461	  `steps.stage: null`.
462	- **Store** (`store.quantities`): the ten quantities of `--measure`, each
463	  with `boundary`, after the stage's last assertion (exact in every
464	  setting), and `peak`, which depends on how often the system takes it
465	  (`--peak-every`, absys-measure `8a0eefd`; QUESTIONS, A15):
466	
467	  | run | `--peak-every` | `peak` |
468	  |---|---|---|
469	  | cost | 0: only when an assertion is added and when its elaboration ends | `null`, with a note: not a peak |
470	  | storage | 1000: every 1000 steps, and at the start and end of each assertion | `kind: "sampled"`, `sample_interval`: "every 1000 steps, and at the start and end of each assertion (absys-measure --peak-every 1000)" |
471	  | storage, `HARNESS_EXACT_PEAK=1` | 1: after every step | `kind: "exact"` |
472	  | either, with a build that rejects `--peak-every` (`5450449`) | not passed: after every step | `kind: "exact"`, as before |
473	
474	  `alternatives.peak` (derivations) follows the same rule. Step counts and
475	  standard output are the same at every setting. A stage with no
476	  assertion has the boundary of the last assertion before it and no peak.
477	- **Suspended work** (`suspended`) is what the system prints as suspended,
478	  in every mode, counted by kind under `--measure`'s names
479	  (`susp_equations` for an equation between unknowns, `susp_applications`
480	  for "waits for a definition" or "for its key", `susp_relations` for
481	  "waits for two of its numbers" or "for its term", `susp_negations` for
482	  "waits for its variables" or "cannot be decided yet"), summed over
483	  derivations. The printer shows only processes still waiting on an
484	  uninstantiated variable; `--measure`'s `susp_*` in the store also count
485	  equations and arithmetic relations that stay associated with their
486	  variables after every one is bound (`docs/decisions.md`, rule 10), so
487	  the two may differ.
488	- **Repeated work** (cost mode, budget 10⁶): `reactivating_events`, the
489	  number of trace events of the stage's assertions that reactivated
490	  suspended processes (`… reactivated …`: a variable was bound and the
491	  processes waiting on it went back to the goal). Not measured (`null`)
492	  where the budget is 10⁸, whose traces would be too large to keep.
493	- **P13**: `cpu_time_s` and `max_rss_kb` of the behaviour run's process
494	  (`getrusage` through `os.wait4`), for growth only.
495	
496	## 5. Budget, safety limit, reposing
497	
498	- **Budget.** `--steps B`, B the problem's budget, is the system's own
499	  budget, and it counts **per assertion**: each assertion is elaborated
500	  for at most B steps. A stage of several assertions can therefore spend
501	  more than B in all before the system reports budget (QUESTIONS, A1);
502	  cost records say so in a note when it happens. A stage is *budget* when
503	  the system's state reports derivations "still elaborating when the
504	  budget ran out".
505	- **Continuing after budget: yes, in every configuration.** The derivations
506	  still elaborating stay in the session, and the next assertion accepted
507	  goes on elaborating them, with a new budget. So after *budget* the next
508	  stage is posed into the same session, `continued_after_budget: true`.
509	- **Safety limit.** For an incremental stage, from writing its first line
510	  to reading the last reply; for a reposed one, the whole run, replay
511	  included. When it is reached the harness sends **SIGKILL** to the
512	  system's process (`safety_limit.how_stopped`), records what it had read,
513	  and, where the problem allows, reruns the stage once with the raised
514	  limit, by reposing (the session is gone). P12, P13 and P16: no rerun.
515	- **Reposing** (after *error*, after a final *timeout*, a safety rerun):
516	  a new session, into which the harness writes the parameters, the
517	  prelude and every section of stages 1 to *k*−1 in order, each followed
518	  by `.help`, replacements and withdrawals included, then stage *k* as
519	  usual. The repl gives no step count, so the restart cost is measured on
520	  a **separate run** of that same text with `absys-measure json`, which
521	  reports each assertion's steps (the same count as `--measure`'s, as the
522	  qualification shows) without sampling the store
523	  (`restart_cost_method: "separate-run"`). It stops at a syntax error,
524	  where the repl goes on, so after an error it may undercount, and the
525	  record says so in `harness_faults`.
526	- **Error.** The repl reports a syntax or static error and goes on; the
527	  harness records the stage as *error* with the message verbatim, and
528	  poses the next stage by reposing, as `PROTOCOL.md` says. A system
529	  process that ends on its own (a crash, or killed by the kernel) is
530	  *error* too, with its exit status or signal.
531	- **When a reposed stage's replay itself cannot finish** (the replay is
532	  killed for lack of memory), no restart cost can be measured, and the
533	  record does not validate: it is kept as `.INVALID.json`, exit 3
534	  (QUESTIONS, A12).
535	
536	## 6. `check`
537	
538	    harnesses/absys/check CONFIGURATION PROGRAM
539	
540	Absys has no parse-only mode. `absys lsp` cannot serve: its diagnostics
541	*run* the text (`src/lsp.rs`, `analyse`, with a budget of 20 000 steps).
542	So `check` does this, the same for every configuration (the flags change
543	nothing a parser sees):
544	
545	1. It reads the program's bytes and finds its sections, as `run` does
546	   (3.1); it reports misplaced markers, numbering, and a missing `AUTHOR`
547	   line (a warning).
548	2. For each section, as the harness would give it, it does what the repl
549	   does line by line (3.2): after each line, it gives the text read since
550	   the last complete assertion to `absys-measure json FILE --steps 0`.
551	   That command parses the text and compiles each assertion and adds it
552	   to the goal, with **a budget of zero steps**: no step of the machine
553	   is taken, so no equation, application, `or`, `not`, `set` or `tout` is
554	   elaborated. `check` reads only the error (with its line and column)
555	   and the number of assertions, and stops if the system reports any step
556	   or event at all.
557	3. It prints each error verbatim, with its line in the program, each line
558	   that the repl would take as a command, and each section that ends in
559	   an unfinished assertion. Exit 0 when there is none, 1 otherwise.
560	
561	It never prints anything the program would compute. The qualification
562	shows it on a program whose only effect, run, is to output a marker: the
563	marker is not in `check`'s output, while running the program prints it.
564	Absys has no means of writing a file, so no file test is possible.
565	
566	## 7. Confounds
567	
568	Everything the harness does beyond passing stages in, collecting answers
569	through the system's mechanism and reading state (copied into every
570	record's `run.confounds`):
571	
572	1. Behaviour runs use the measurement build with `--full` (printer only),
573	   not the baseline build (2).
574	2. The `.help` line after each section, to know where the system's output
575	   for it ends; a section ending inside an unfinished assertion turns it
576	   into a syntax error (3.2).
577	3. `?` and `? NAME` to read the state (3.8).
578	4. The parameters' assertions, written by the harness (3.4).
579	5. PART sections chosen by the instance's order (3.5).
580	6. Spawned computations accepted one after another into the one session,
581	   each read right after its section (3.6).
582	7. The budget is per assertion (5).
583	8. Cost and storage runs are a new process per stage, on stages 1..k (3.2).
584	9. The restart cost of a reposed behaviour stage is measured on a separate
585	   `json` run (5).
586	10. The trace is switched on in P11 runs and in cost runs with the 10⁶
587	    budget (3.10, 4).
588	11. `answers(cap)` takes the first `cap` derivations of the printed state (3.7).
589	12. Each constant's name is replaced by its value in the section that uses
590	    it, when that section is given; the block itself is never given (3.9).
591	
592	## 8. Qualification
593	
594	`qualification/run-qualification` reruns everything; its output is
595	`qualification/output.txt`, and its records are in
596	`qualification/records/`. See [`qualification/README.md`](qualification/README.md).
597	# S mechanisms of the Absys configurations
598	
599	*`PROTOCOL.md`, "Recording a result": every configuration's S mechanisms
600	are listed, with their size, before any program is run. `METRICS.md`,
601	class S: code that implements a mechanism the configuration lacks,
602	counted once per mechanism per configuration.*
603	
604	| configuration | S mechanisms | size |
605	|---|---|---|
606	| `absys` | none | 0 tokens |
607	| `absys-depth-first` | none | 0 tokens |
608	| `absys-wake-back` | none | 0 tokens |
609	
610	**Why none.** The systems file: "Nothing else exists to be imported, so
611	every Absys configuration has no external mechanisms." Absys has no
612	library, no import and no foreign call, and this harness provides none:
613	it gives the system the program's text, its own commands (`.help`, `?`,
614	`? NAME`, `.trace`) and the parameters' assertions (README, 3.4), none of
615	which is a mechanism a program can use to compute. The binding of emit is
616	`tout`, a primitive of the core (systems file, "The core"), and is H, not
617	S (README, 3.12).
618	
619	So any supporting code a program for Absys needs (a scheduler, a
620	wait-for-definition layer, a hand-written search) can only be written in
621	the program itself, in Absys. It is then S counted against that
622	configuration under `METRICS.md`, rule 12, once per mechanism, with the
623	problems that use it listed, and this file lists nothing for it in
624	advance.

% before it is defined, and a prime introduces a new name (Foster and Elcock 1969; docs/decisions.md rule 6), so the definition

% AUTHOR: implementation-absys (an agent: Claude Opus 5.5, claude-opus-5-5). One text for absys, absys-depth-first and absys-wake-back.
% PRECURSOR-SEEN: no. Not any E01-E09 program (see programs/absys/README.md, batch 1B, for what was read).
% NOTATION: 1969 (.ab1), the earliest notation with every construct used (systems/absys/README.md, Notation), as for rev and conc in P03.
% IDIOM: a relation as a lambda whose body is {A or B}, primes for new local names, lists [a;b] and [h&t]: Foster and Elcock 1969 (map and item, examples/map.ab1, examples/triples.ab1);
% IDIOM: the shape of the two cases, {R = [], S = T} or {R = [X|L], T = [X|N], app(L, S, N)}: Elcock 1990 p. 8 (examples/append.abs);
% IDIOM: an application of a procedure that has no value yet waits for it: Elcock 1990 p. 10 (docs/decisions.md rule 6; tutorial ch. 4).
% The procedure names are written without a prime where they are defined (rev=lambda, not rev'=lambda): the name is applied
% before it is defined, and a prime introduces a new name (Foster and Elcock 1969; docs/decisions.md rule 6), so the definition
% must be an equation on the name already in use. No declaration changes how an undefined relation behaves (there is none).
% P08c. Unknown b. Stage 1 the definition of conc; stage 2 rev(<seq>, b); stage 3 rev, case 1 only; stage 4 rev, case 2.
% REFORMULATION (R): an Absys procedure is one value, given by one equation (docs/decisions.md rule 6), and has no means of
% receiving a further case. So rev's definition at stage 3 is its case 1 or an application of revmore, a name for the cases
% not yet given, which waits for its definition (rule 6). Stage 4 defines revmore as case 2. revmore, its alternative in rev
% and its definition's head are R; the cases' contents are the problem's. The literal reading, two equations on rev, is the
% named variant variants/P08c.redefine.ab1.
% CONSTANTS BEGIN
rs = [1;2]   % stage 2: rev(rs, b)
r1p = []   % stage 3: case 1, rev(r1p, r1r)
r1r = []   % stage 3: case 1, rev(r1p, r1r)
% CONSTANTS END
% STAGE 1
% conc, P03 Vocabulary, cases 1 and 2 in that order; case 2 as its head equations, then conc(a, b, c).
conc=lambda p, q, r
    begin {p = [] q = r or
           p = [h'&k'] r = [h&m'] conc(k, q, m)} end
% STAGE 2
rev(rs, b)
% STAGE 3
% rev, P03 Vocabulary, case 1 only: rev(<>, <>), as equations on the parameters; then the cases still to come (R).
rev=lambda p, r
    begin {p = r1p r = r1r or
           revmore(p, r)} end
% STAGE 4
% rev, P03 Vocabulary, case 2: its head equation, then rev(l, q), then conc(q, <h>, r), as the definition of revmore (R).
revmore=lambda p, r
    begin p = [h'&k'] rev(k, n') conc(n, [h], r) end

% AUTHOR: implementation-absys (an agent: Claude Opus 5.5, claude-opus-5-5). One text for absys, absys-depth-first and absys-wake-back.
% PRECURSOR-SEEN: no. Not any E01-E09 program (see programs/absys/README.md, batch 1B, for what was read).
% NAMED VARIANT, not the primary (the primary is P06d.abs): setdiff stated with the set-forming construct, as P06d allows.
% Not chosen as primary: set gives the distinct values of X, so for an s1 with a repeated element it is not the problem's setdiff,
% and the order of its list is the order in which the derivations stand (docs/decisions.md rule 19), not the problem's case analysis.
% NOTATION: 1990 (.abs), the earliest notation with not (systems/absys/README.md, Notation; docs/decisions.md rule 18).
% IDIOM: not(A), an independent computation with the criteria reversed: Elcock 1990 p. 14 (tutorial ch. 7: not(X = 1)).
% IDIOM: setdiff = lambda S1, S2, S {set(X), {mem(X, S1), not(mem(X, S2))}, S}: Elcock 1990 p. 15, a demonstration of Absys-4 (examples/setdiff.abs; tutorial ch. 7);
% IDIOM: mem written as {S = [X|T]} or {S = [Y|T], mem(X, T)}: the reconstruction's own mem (tutorial ch. 7, examples/setdiff.abs).
% P06d. Unknown d. One stage: setdiff(<seq>, <seq>, d).
% CONSTANTS BEGIN
s1v = [1, 2, 3, 4]   % stage 1: s1
s2v = [2, 4, 6]   % stage 1: s2
% CONSTANTS END
% mem, P06d, cases 1 and 2 in that order: mem(e, <e> ++ t); mem(e, <h> ++ t) if mem(e, t). Each head as an equation on the lambda's parameter.
mem = lambda E, S
    {S = [E|T]} or
    {S = [H|T], mem(E, T)}
% setdiff, P06d, as a set former: d is the elements of s1 that are not elements of s2 (METRICS.md rule 7).
setdiff = lambda S1, S2, D
    {set(X), {mem(X, S1), not(mem(X, S2))}, D}
% STAGE 1
setdiff(s1v, s2v, d)

# Residual-equivalence check for P08a stages 4 and 5 (all three configurations print the same state).
# The system's state: bindings plus suspended equations between unknowns. We close the equations with
# union-find and substitute into a and b, then compare with the valid outcomes up to renaming of the
# free representatives.
def solve(bindings, eqs):
    parent={}
    def f(v):
        parent.setdefault(v,v)
        while parent[v]!=v: v=parent[v]
        return v
    for a,b in eqs: parent[f(a)]=f(b)
    sub=lambda t:[f(e) for e in t]
    return {k:sub(v) for k,v in bindings.items()}, f
def canon(lists):
    names={}; out=[]
    for l in lists:
        out.append([names.setdefault(e,'V%d'%len(names)) for e in l])
    return out
# stage 4: a = [x;y;z], b = [h5;h6;h1]; suspended x=y, x=h1, y=h2, z=h3, h3=h4, h4=h5, h2=h6
b4={'a':['x','y','z'],'b':['h5','h6','h1']}
e4=[('x','y'),('x','h1'),('y','h2'),('z','h3'),('h3','h4'),('h4','h5'),('h2','h6')]
r,f=solve(b4,e4)
sys4=canon([r['a'],r['b'],[f('x'),f('y'),f('z')]])
# valid stage 4: x = y, a = <y,y,z>, b = <z,y,y>
val4=canon([['y','y','z'],['z','y','y'],['y','y','z']])
print('stage 4 system',sys4,'valid',val4,'equivalent',sys4==val4)
# stage 5: add y = z
e5=e4+[('y','z')]
r,f=solve(b4,e5)
sys5=canon([r['a'],r['b'],[f('x'),f('y'),f('z')]])
val5=canon([['z','z','z'],['z','z','z'],['z','z','z']])
print('stage 5 system',sys5,'valid',val5,'equivalent',sys5==val5)
EOF

# Builds absys.json for classifier A, absys batch 1B (P04, P06, P07, P08).
# Run: python3 -I build.py REPO OUTDIR
import json, glob, os, sys, csv

REPO, OUT = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
CONFIGS = ['absys', 'absys-depth-first', 'absys-wake-back']
TOK = os.path.join(REPO, 'results/absys/tokens')

def ntok(rel):
    with open(os.path.join(TOK, 'absys', rel + '.tokens.tsv')) as f:
        return sum(1 for _ in f) - 1

def P(a, b, c, rule='rule 1 (reference semantics): part of the problem as given'):
    return {'from': a, 'to': b, 'class': 'P', 'construct': c, 'rule': rule}
def R(a, b, c, rule):
    return {'from': a, 'to': b, 'class': 'R', 'construct': c, 'rule': rule}

CONST = 'rule 1: a constant of the stage information, in the constants block (harness README 3.9); removing it changes the posed information'
SEP = 'rule 20: the separator takes the class of the construct that follows'

spans = {}
# ---------------- P04
for f, q in [('P04a.ab1', 'query: loop(x) or x = 1, in that order (P04a), a disjunction the problem states (rule 6)'),
             ('P04b.ab1', 'query: x = 1 or loop(x), in that order (P04b), a disjunction the problem states (rule 6)')]:
    spans[f] = [P(0, 3, "loop's definition: its head, loop'=lambda p"),
                P(4, 9, "loop, case 1: loop(x) if loop(x), the body begin loop(p) end"),
                P(10, 12, 'constant xval = 1 (stage 1)', CONST),
                P(13, 22, q)]
for f, query in [('P04c.ab1', True), ('P04d.ab1', False)]:
    s = [P(0, 3, "alist-left: definition head alist'=lambda p"),
         P(4, 5, 'alist-left: begin { opening the disjunction of its cases'),
         P(6, 16, "alist-left, case 1: alist(m') and p = ['a'&m], conjuncts in the order written (head as an equation on the parameter)"),
         P(17, 21, 'alist-left, case 2: or p = [] (alist(<>))', 'rule 1; ' + SEP),
         P(22, 23, 'alist-left: } end closing the definition')]
    if query:
        s += [P(24, 30, "constant sq = ['a';'a'] (stage 1)", CONST), P(31, 34, 'query: alist(sq), P04c')]
    else:
        s += [P(24, 27, 'query: alist(s), P04d')]
    spans[f] = s
for f, query in [('P04e.ab1', True), ('P04f.ab1', False)]:
    s = [P(0, 3, "alist-right: definition head alist'=lambda p"),
         P(4, 5, 'alist-right: begin { opening the disjunction of its cases'),
         P(6, 9, 'alist-right, case 1: p = [] (alist(<>))'),
         P(10, 21, "alist-right, case 2: or p = ['a'&m'] alist(m) (head as an equation, then alist(m))", 'rule 1; ' + SEP),
         P(22, 23, 'alist-right: } end closing the definition')]
    if query:
        s += [P(24, 30, "constant sq = ['a';'a'] (stage 1)", CONST), P(31, 34, 'query: alist(sq), P04e')]
    else:
        s += [P(24, 27, 'query: alist(s), P04f')]
    spans[f] = s
# ---------------- P06a-c
spans['P06a.abs'] = [P(0, 2, 'constant nk1 = 1 (stage 1)', CONST), P(3, 5, 'constant xk2 = 2 (stage 2)', CONST),
                     P(6, 11, 'stage 1: not(x = nk1), negation the problem states'), P(12, 14, 'stage 2: x = xk2')]
spans['P06b.abs'] = [P(0, 2, 'constant xk1 = 2 (stage 1)', CONST), P(3, 5, 'constant nk2 = 1 (stage 2)', CONST),
                     P(6, 8, 'stage 1: x = xk1'), P(9, 14, 'stage 2: not(x = nk2), negation the problem states')]
spans['P06c.abs'] = [P(0, 2, 'constant nk1 = 1 (stage 1)', CONST), P(3, 5, 'constant xk2 = 1 (stage 2)', CONST),
                     P(6, 11, 'stage 1: not(x = nk1), negation the problem states'), P(12, 14, 'stage 2: x = xk2')]
mem = [P(20, 25, 'mem: definition head mem = lambda E, S'),
       P(26, 34, 'mem, case 1: {S = [E|T]} (mem(e, <e> ++ t)), head as an equation on the parameter'),
       P(35, 51, 'mem, case 2: or {S = [H|T], mem(E, T)}', 'rule 1; ' + SEP)]
consts_d = [P(0, 10, 'constant s1v = [1, 2, 3, 4] (stage 1)', CONST), P(11, 19, 'constant s2v = [2, 4, 6] (stage 1)', CONST)]
spans['P06d.abs'] = consts_d + mem + [
    P(52, 59, 'setdiff: definition head setdiff = lambda S1, S2, D'),
    P(60, 70, 'setdiff, case 1: {S1 = [], D = []}'),
    P(71, 96, 'setdiff, case 2: or {S1 = [H|T], mem(H, S2), setdiff(T, S2, D)}', 'rule 1; ' + SEP),
    P(97, 133, 'setdiff, case 3: or {S1 = [H|T], D = [H|R], not(mem(H, S2)), setdiff(T, S2, R)}', 'rule 1; ' + SEP),
    P(134, 141, 'stage 1 query: setdiff(s1v, s2v, d)')]
spans['variants/P06d.set.abs'] = consts_d + mem + [
    P(52, 59, 'setdiff: definition head setdiff = lambda S1, S2, D'),
    P(60, 86, 'setdiff as a set former: {set(X), {mem(X, S1), not(mem(X, S2))}, D}', 'rule 7: a set-forming construct stating the definition the problem gives is P (P06d says so)'),
    P(87, 94, 'stage 1 query: setdiff(s1v, s2v, d)')]
def students(off_who):
    names = [('st1', "student fact 1"), ('st2', 'student fact 2'), ('mc1', 'maths fact 1'), ('mc2', 'maths fact 2'),
             ('tp1', 'takes fact 1, person'), ('tc1', 'takes fact 1, course'), ('tp2', 'takes fact 2, person'),
             ('tc2', 'takes fact 2, course'), ('tp3', 'takes fact 3, person'), ('tc3', 'takes fact 3, course')]
    s = []
    i = 0
    for n, d in names:
        s.append(P(i, i + 2, 'constant %s (%s)' % (n, d), CONST)); i += 3
    if off_who:
        s.append(P(i, i + 2, "constant who (the query's atom)", CONST)); i += 3
    b = i
    F = 'rule 6: a set of facts the problem states, in a closed world, as a procedure whose alternatives are the facts'
    s += [P(b, b + 3, 'student: definition head student = lambda P', F),
          P(b + 4, b + 8, 'student fact 1: {P = st1}', F),
          P(b + 9, b + 14, 'student fact 2: or {P = st2}', F + '; ' + SEP),
          P(b + 15, b + 18, 'maths: definition head maths = lambda K', F),
          P(b + 19, b + 23, 'maths fact 1: {K = mc1}', F),
          P(b + 24, b + 29, 'maths fact 2: or {K = mc2}', F + '; ' + SEP),
          P(b + 30, b + 35, 'takes: definition head takes = lambda P, K', F),
          P(b + 36, b + 45, 'takes fact 1: {P = tp1, K = tc1} or', F),
          P(b + 46, b + 55, 'takes fact 2: {P = tp2, K = tc2} or', F),
          P(b + 56, b + 64, 'takes fact 3: {P = tp3, K = tc3}', F),
          P(b + 65, b + 68, 'nonmajor: definition head nonmajor = lambda P'),
          P(b + 69, b + 89, 'nonmajor, case 1: {student(P), maths(K), not(takes(P, K))}, conjuncts in the order written')]
    q = b + 90
    return s, q
for f, who in [('P06e1.abs', True), ('P06e2.abs', True), ('P06e3.abs', False)]:
    s, q = students(who)
    s.append(P(q, q + 3, 'stage 1 query: nonmajor(%s)' % ('who' if who else 'p')))
    spans[f] = s
# The 'or' separators inside takes are written at the end of each fact's line (tokens 78, 88 in P06e1):
# fact spans above include the trailing 'or'. Rule 20 would give each 'or' to the following fact; both are P,
# so the class is unaffected.
# ---------------- P07
def p07(f, consts, cnames):
    toks = [l.rstrip('\n').split('\t') for l in open(os.path.join(TOK, 'absys', f + '.tokens.tsv'))][1:]
    s = []
    for i, (a, b, c) in enumerate(consts):
        s.append(P(a, b, 'constant ' + c, CONST))
    start = consts[-1][1] + 1
    texts = [t[2] for t in toks]
    n = len(texts)
    grouped = texts[start] == 'begin'
    i = start
    if grouped:
        s.append(P(start, start, 'begin: the stage\'s relations as one conjunction (opening)', 'rule 1: the conjunction connective of the stage'))
        i = start + 1
    end = n - 2 if grouped else n - 1
    r0 = i
    for j in range(i, end + 1):
        if texts[j] in cnames:
            s.append(P(r0, j, 'relation: ' + ' '.join(texts[r0:j + 1]) + ' (a compound expression is a transcription, SPECIFICATION Conventions)'))
            r0 = j + 1
    if grouped:
        s.append(P(n - 1, n - 1, 'end: closing the conjunction', 'rule 1: the conjunction connective of the stage'))
    return s
a_consts = [(0, 2, 'r1sum = 12 (relation 1)'), (3, 5, 'r2sum = 7 (relation 2)'), (6, 8, 'r3val = 3 (relation 3)')]
for f in ['P07a.ab1', 'P07a.132.ab1', 'P07a.213.ab1', 'P07a.231.ab1', 'P07a.312.ab1', 'P07a.321.ab1']:
    spans[f] = p07(f, a_consts, {'r1sum', 'r2sum', 'r3val'})
spans['P07b.ab1'] = p07('P07b.ab1', [(0, 2, 'bsum = 10'), (3, 5, 'bdiff = 4')], {'bsum', 'bdiff'})
spans['P07c.ab1'] = p07('P07c.ab1', [(0, 2, 'csum = 10')], {'csum'})
spans['P07d.ab1'] = p07('P07d.ab1', [(0, 2, 'uval = 2'), (3, 5, 'vval = 14')], {'v', 'uval', 'vval'})
spans['P07e.ab1'] = p07('P07e.ab1', [(0, 2, 'uval = 2'), (3, 5, 'vval = 15')], {'v', 'uval', 'vval'})
spans['P07f.ab1'] = p07('P07f.ab1', [(0, 2, 'fsum1 = 10'), (3, 5, 'fsum2 = 11')], {'fsum1', 'fsum2'})
spans['P07g.ab1'] = p07('P07g.ab1', [(0, 2, 'gsq = 9')], {'gsq'})
# ---------------- P08
concdef = lambda b: [P(b, b + 7, 'conc: definition head conc=lambda p, q, r (no prime: an equation on the name, Absys idiom)'),
                     P(b + 8, b + 9, 'conc: begin { opening its cases'),
                     P(b + 10, b + 16, 'conc, case 1: p = [] q = r'),
                     P(b + 17, b + 39, "conc, case 2: or p = [h'&k'] r = [h&m'] conc(k, q, m)", 'rule 1; ' + SEP),
                     P(b + 40, b + 41, 'conc: } end')]
spans['P08a.ab1'] = [P(0, 2, 'constant pfx = 42 (stage 6)', CONST),
                     P(3, 11, 'stage 1: a = [x;y;z]'),
                     P(12, 17, 'stage 2: rev(a, b), the application before any definition'),
                     P(18, 20, 'stage 3: x = y'),
                     P(21, 26, 'stage 4: rev definition head rev=lambda p, r (no prime: the definition is information equated with the name already applied)'),
                     P(27, 28, 'rev: begin {'),
                     P(29, 36, 'rev, case 1: p = [] r = []'),
                     P(37, 60, "rev, case 2: or p = [h'&k'] rev(k, n') conc(n, [h], r), conjuncts in the order written", 'rule 1; ' + SEP),
                     P(61, 62, 'rev: } end')] + concdef(63) + [
                     P(105, 107, 'stage 5: y = z'),
                     P(108, 114, 'stage 6: b = [pfx&c]')]
spans['P08b.ab1'] = [P(0, 8, 'stage 1: a = [x;y;z]'), P(9, 14, 'stage 2: rev(a, b)'), P(15, 17, 'stage 3: x = y')]
c_consts = [P(0, 6, 'constant rs = [1;2] (stage 2)', CONST), P(7, 10, 'constant r1p = [] (stage 3, case 1)', CONST),
            P(11, 14, 'constant r1r = [] (stage 3, case 1)', CONST)]
spans['P08c.ab1'] = c_consts + concdef(15) + [
    P(57, 62, 'stage 2: rev(rs, b), before rev has a definition'),
    P(63, 68, 'stage 3: rev definition head rev=lambda p, r'),
    P(69, 70, 'rev: begin {'),
    P(71, 76, 'rev, case 1: p = r1p r = r1r (rev(<>, <>))'),
    R(77, 83, 'or revmore(p, r): an alternative standing for the cases of rev not yet given, which waits for its definition',
      'R: a case the problem file does not give (METRICS class R; rule 4 for the tokens that introduce it); ' + SEP),
    P(84, 85, "rev: } end, closing rev's definition"),
    R(86, 92, 'stage 4: revmore=lambda p, r begin, the head of a definition the problem does not give (revmore)',
      'rule 4: the tokens that introduce the case moved into a new procedure are R; the contents are classed on their own (rule 10)'),
    P(93, 115, "rev, case 2 contents: p = [h'&k'] rev(k, n') conc(n, [h], r), as the problem's case 2", 'rule 10: nested construct classed on its own; the case is the problem\'s'),
    R(116, 116, "end closing revmore's definition", 'rule 4: the tokens that close the reformulated case are R')]
spans['variants/P08c.redefine.ab1'] = c_consts + concdef(15) + [
    P(57, 62, 'stage 2: rev(rs, b), before rev has a definition'),
    P(63, 68, 'stage 3: rev definition head rev=lambda p, r (case 1 alone)'),
    P(69, 76, 'rev, case 1: begin p = r1p r = r1r end'),
    P(77, 82, 'stage 4: a second equation on rev, rev=lambda p, r (case 2 alone)', 'rule 1: the stage information transcribed literally (its meaning in Absys is a second equation on rev: see notes)'),
    P(83, 107, "rev, case 2: begin p = [h'&k'] rev(k, n') conc(n, [h], r) end")]

# ---------- check coverage
texts = [l.rstrip('\n').split('\t') for l in open(os.path.join(TOK, 'TEXTS-1B-P04-P06-P08.tsv'))][1:]
tokens_out = {}
for t, also in texts:
    rel = t.split('/', 1)[1]
    n = ntok(rel)
    sp = sorted(spans[rel], key=lambda s: s['from'])
    cov = []
    for s in sp:
        cov += list(range(s['from'], s['to'] + 1))
    assert cov == list(range(n)), (rel, n, [(s['from'], s['to']) for s in sp])
    tokens_out[t] = sp
assert len(tokens_out) == len(spans)

# ---------- records
def recs(conf, prob):
    out = {}
    for f in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(REPO, 'results/absys', conf, prob, 'raw', '*.json'))):
        d = json.load(open(f))
        prog = d['run']['program']['path'].split('/', 3)[3]
        out[(d['run']['instance'], prog, d['run']['mode'])] = os.path.relpath(f, REPO)
    for f in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(REPO, 'results/absys', conf, prob, 'raw-rerun-m2', '*.json'))):
        d = json.load(open(f))
        prog = d['run']['program']['path'].split('/', 3)[3]
        out[(d['run']['instance'], prog, d['run']['mode'] + '-m2')] = os.path.relpath(f, REPO)
    return out

def O(sem, rep, simp=None, ident=None, size=None, ex=('finished',), eq=None, obs='', rule=None, **kw):
    d = {'reached': True, 'semantic': sem, 'representation': rep, 'simplification': simp,
         'identical_to_posed': ident, 'residual_size': size, 'execution_state': list(ex),
         'residual_equivalence': eq, 'observations': obs, 'rule': rule}
    d.update(kw)
    return d

NOMAN = ' Manual actions: none. No earlier conclusion withdrawn.'
B = {}  # (instance, program) -> list of stage dicts, for the configuration absys (others differ only where stated)
B[('P04a', 'P04a.ab1')] = [O('complete', 'explicit', ex=('budget',),
    eq='Derivation #2 binds x = 1. Derivation #1 still holds loop(x) to do; loop, read as the least relation, has no instances, so the two derivations together denote exactly x = 1.',
    obs='x = 1 is reported (derivation #2, hibernating), beside derivation #1, still elaborating loop(x) when the budget ran out (x uninstantiated). Alternatives: 2 derivations, all live, at the boundary and at the budget. Suspended work: none (0). The endless alternative did not hide the finite one. Steps (cost run): 1000002.' + NOMAN,
    rule='SPECIFICATION Outcomes 2: classified on the more explicit valid form (x = 1); the still-elaborating derivation is recorded as an observation. Execution state budget: the system reports a derivation still elaborating when the budget ran out.')]
B[('P04b', 'P04b.ab1')] = [O('complete', 'explicit', ex=('budget',),
    eq='Derivation #1 binds x = 1; derivation #2 holds loop(x) to do, which has no instances under the least relation, so the report denotes exactly x = 1.',
    obs='x = 1 is reported first (derivation #1, hibernating); derivation #2 still elaborating loop(x) at the budget. Alternatives: 2 derivations, all live. Suspended work: none. Steps (cost run): 1000002.' + NOMAN,
    rule='SPECIFICATION Outcomes 2 (more explicit valid form); budget as reported.')]
for inst, prog, defn in [('P04c', 'P04c.ab1', 'alist-left'), ('P04e', 'P04e.ab1', 'alist-right')]:
    B[(inst, prog)] = [O('complete', 'explicit',
        eq=None,
        obs='One derivation survives, hibernating, with no unknowns (true). The computation finishes. Alternatives: 1 derivation at the boundary (peak 2 in the storage run; peak 4 under absys-depth-first for P04c). Suspended work: none. Steps (cost run): 15. Definition: %s.' % defn + NOMAN,
        rule='SPECIFICATION Outcomes 1, 2: true with no unknowns, one solution given (the empty assignment).')]
for inst, prog, defn in [('P04d', 'P04d.ab1', 'alist-left'), ('P04f', 'P04f.ab1', 'alist-right')]:
    B[(inst, prog)] = [O('none reported', None, ex=('error',),
        eq=None,
        obs='The system process was ended by SIGKILL (exit -9), which the harness did not send: the record attributes it to the container\'s memory, the system keeping every event of its run (about 85 bytes a step). No state was printed, so no solution of the infinitely many is reported, and whether every solution would be reached given enough steps cannot be read from the record. Alternatives and suspended work: unavailable (not 0, AMENDMENTS 3.1). Definition: %s. Answer completeness (infinite outcomes): no finite equivalent representation; no answers obtained.' % defn + NOMAN,
        rule='SPECIFICATION Outcomes 3, error, verbatim in the record; nothing reported, so none reported.')]
B[('P06a', 'P06a.abs')] = [
    O('unsound', 'explicit',
      obs='The system reports that no derivation survives ("the assertions are unsatisfiable") where every x other than 1 is valid. The negation was decided at once, in stage 1, at step 5 (cost run): not(x = 1) started an independent computation (#1), which bound its own x to 1 and hibernated without contradiction, so the not failed. It was not held as a condition, not delayed, not an error. Unknown x: no derivation, so no representation. Alternatives: 0 derivations (peak 1; sub_derivations peak 1). Suspended work: none (susp_negations 0).' + NOMAN,
      rule='SPECIFICATION Outcomes 1, unsound: reports there are none where valid outcomes exist (P06 Observations: a system that reports no solution for P06a is unsound).'),
    O('unsound', 'explicit',
      obs='No derivation survives from stage 1; x = 2 has nothing to act on (0 steps at stage 2). Valid outcome x = 2 is not reported. P06a and P06b do not give the same outcome. Alternatives: 0. Suspended work: none.' + NOMAN,
      rule='SPECIFICATION Outcomes 1, unsound: reports none where x = 2 is valid.')]
B[('P06b', 'P06b.abs')] = [
    O('complete', 'explicit', obs='x = 2, one derivation, hibernating. Alternatives: 1. Suspended work: none.' + NOMAN, rule='SPECIFICATION Outcomes 1, 2.'),
    O('complete', 'explicit', obs='x = 2. The negation was decided at stage 2, at once, with x known: its independent computation failed on 2 = 1, so not(x = 1) holds (sub_derivations peak 1, 4 steps). Alternatives: 1. Suspended work: none.' + NOMAN, rule='SPECIFICATION Outcomes 1, 2.')]
B[('P06c', 'P06c.abs')] = [
    O('unsound', 'explicit', obs='As P06a stage 1: not(x = 1) decided at once at step 5, failing because its independent computation could bind x to 1; the system reports that no derivation survives where every x other than 1 is valid. Alternatives: 0. Suspended work: none.' + NOMAN,
      rule='SPECIFICATION Outcomes 1, unsound.'),
    O('complete', 'explicit', obs='No derivation survives, which matches the valid outcome (none), but only because the computation had already failed at stage 1 (0 steps at stage 2); the inconsistency of x = 1 with not(x = 1) was never itself detected. Answer completeness: the system reported that there are none (yes). Alternatives: 0. Suspended work: none.' + NOMAN,
      rule='SPECIFICATION Outcomes 1, complete: the report (none) equals the valid outcomes (none).')]
B[('P06d', 'P06d.abs')] = [O('complete', 'explicit',
    obs='d = [1,3], one derivation surviving (derivation #94 under absys and absys-wake-back, #43 under absys-depth-first). Each not(mem(H, S2)) is decided with H and S2 known. Alternatives: 1 at the boundary; peak 12 derivations and 34 sub-derivations (absys, absys-wake-back), 7 and 16 (absys-depth-first). Suspended work: none. Steps (cost): 405 (399 depth-first). Answer completeness 1/1, 0 invalid.' + NOMAN,
    rule='SPECIFICATION Outcomes 1, 2.')]
B[('P06d', 'variants/P06d.set.abs')] = [O('complete', 'explicit',
    obs='Named variant (set former). d = [1,3], one derivation. Alternatives: 1 (peak 1; sub_derivations peak 9, 6 depth-first). Suspended work: none. Steps (cost): 198 (192 depth-first). Answer completeness 1/1.' + NOMAN,
    rule='SPECIFICATION Outcomes 1, 2.')]
B[('P06e1', 'P06e1.abs')] = [O('complete', 'explicit',
    obs='True: one derivation survives with no unknowns. Ground negations only (p and k known before each not). Alternatives: 1 (peak 2; 3 depth-first). Suspended work: none.' + NOMAN, rule='SPECIFICATION Outcomes 1, 2.')]
B[('P06e2', 'P06e2.abs')] = [O('complete', 'explicit',
    obs='False: no derivation survives, the valid outcome. Answer completeness: reported that there are none (yes). Alternatives: 0 (peak 2). Suspended work: none.' + NOMAN, rule='SPECIFICATION Outcomes 1: the report (none) equals the valid outcome (false).')]
B[('P06e3', 'P06e3.abs')] = [O('complete', 'explicit',
    obs="p = 'BROWN', one derivation. The trace (cost run) shows student(p) and maths(K) distributed into four derivations, each binding p and k before its not(takes(p, k)) began: p and k are known before the negation is decided. Alternatives: 1 at the boundary (peak 4; 3 depth-first). Suspended work: none. Answer completeness 1/1." + NOMAN,
    rule='SPECIFICATION Outcomes 1, 2.')]
for inst in ['P07a', 'P07a.132', 'P07a.213', 'P07a.231', 'P07a.312', 'P07a.321']:
    B[(inst, inst + '.ab1')] = [O('complete', 'explicit',
        obs='x = 5, y = 4, z = 3, one derivation, finished. Solved one relation at a time as its values became known: the arithmetic relations suspend ("waits for two of its numbers") and are reactivated as z, then the others, are bound (propagation through suspension, not elimination or search). Alternatives: 1. Suspended work at the boundary: none printed (storage susp_relations boundary counts relations still associated with bound variables, harness README 4).' + NOMAN,
        rule='SPECIFICATION Outcomes 1, 2.')]
B[('P07b', 'P07b.ab1')] = [O('complete', 'residual', 'reducible', True,
    'residual: 2 relations (x + y = 10; 4 + y = x), 4 occurrences of unknowns; input: 2 relations (x + y = 10; x - y = 4), 4 occurrences',
    ex=('suspended',),
    eq='The residual x + y = 10, 4 + y = x is x + y = 10, x - y = 4 rewritten (x - y = 4 iff 4 + y = x over the integers), so it denotes exactly x = 7, y = 3. Reducible: x = 7, y = 3 has no relation left to decide.',
    obs='x and y uninstantiated; 2 suspended relations, each "waits for two of its numbers". The system does not eliminate between relations. Alternatives: 1 derivation.' + NOMAN,

# Classifier A: absys, batch 1B (P04, P06, P07, P08). Notes

Classifier A, a Claude agent (claude-opus-5-5), working on the clone at
commit b73d59a. `absys.json` is generated by `build.py` in this folder
(`python3 -I build.py REPO OUTDIR`). The build checks that every token of
every text is covered exactly once, and that each stage's execution state
as classed agrees with the record. Other scripts here: `summ.py` and
`compact.py` (read records), `cmpcfg.py` (compares configurations),
`cmpmode.py` (compares modes with the behaviour run), and `check_p08a.py`
(residual equivalence for P08a, stages 4 and 5).

The brief's file name says P04, P06 and P08, but its text names P07 as well,
and `TEXTS-1B-P04-P06-P08.tsv` lists the P07 texts. I classed all four
problems.

## Tokens

30 texts and 1436 tokens. Every text is shared by the three
configurations, and no class differs between them: no configuration has
an S mechanism, and the programs contain no configuration-specific
construct. So each text is classed once, under its `absys/` path.

Hard or debatable constructs:

1. **The constants block** (`% CONSTANTS BEGIN` … `END`). The harness
   never gives it to the system. It substitutes each value into the
   section that uses it. Its lines are not comments, so the tokenizer
   counts them. I classed them **P** (rule 1): they are the information of
   each stage, and they are the only place a value appears. They are not
   H: harness README 3.12 says only `tout("emit", …)` is H. Someone else
   could reasonably argue for H, since the harness reads the table. If
   they did, the P totals would fall by about 25% in P06e and P07.
2. **P08c, `revmore`** (R tokens 77–83, 86–92 and 116; 15 R tokens in
   all). The program gives rev at stage 3 as case 1 *or* `revmore(p, r)`,
   and defines `revmore` as case 2 at stage 4. I classed the alternative
   `or revmore(p, r)` as R, because it is a case the problem does not
   give; the `or` goes with it by rule 20. I classed revmore's head
   (`revmore=lambda p, r begin`) and its closing `end` as R by rule 4.
   Case 2's contents (93–115) are P by rule 10. The `{`, `}` and `end` of
   rev's own definition are P. **Possible anticipation:** the stage-3 code
   names a procedure for cases "not yet given", so it presumes that more
   cases may come. The problem's open reading itself says "case 2 may yet
   arrive", and the program does not depend on what stage 4 contains. So I
   do not count it as a breach of rule 5, but I flag it.
3. **P08c.redefine** (named variant). It is all P: each stage's part of
   the definition is transcribed literally. It changes the meaning
   because Absys treats a definition as an equation on a name. No token
   does it.
4. **P06d.set** (named variant). I classed the set former as P by rule 7,
   which P06d permits. It is not equivalent to the problem's setdiff for
   an s1 with repeated elements, or for one whose order differs from the
   order of its derivations. That matters for hidden variants, not for
   the class.
5. **P07a in six orders.** Each order is an instance the problem poses,
   so it is P and not a move (rule 4). The `begin … end` grouping is P, as
   the conjunction connective. The compound `x + y + z = 12` is a
   transcription (SPECIFICATION, Conventions).
6. **P06e facts as procedures** (`student = lambda P {P = st1} or {P =
   st2}`). P by rule 6: a set of facts the problem states, in a closed
   world. I gave each `or` between facts to the following fact (rule 20).
7. **P06d mem, case 1: `S = [E|T]`.** Here T ranges over every value,
   where the problem says "for every sequence t". This makes no difference
   on the inputs used. I classed it P as a transcription, but it is a
   (harmless) widening.

## Outcomes

There are 138 stage entries: 46 stages in each of the 3 configurations
(30 programs in each, the 2 named variants included). There are no
`*.INVALID.json` records and no harness faults. Every stage was reached.
The other two configurations print the same state as `absys` (up to the
numbering of derivations) except in **P04a under absys-depth-first**
(`cmpcfg.py`).

Hard cases:

1. **P04a, absys-depth-first.** Both derivations were still elaborating
   at the budget. Derivation #2 holds `x = 1` still *to do*, and `? x`
   says "x does not occur". I classed it as *complete / residual /
   reducible*, identical to the posed information, with *budget*. The
   reasoning: it is state the system holds and would act on, observe()
   reads it, and the specification's examples (P07f) count held, posed
   relations as reported. **Alternative:** *none reported*, since no
   binding of x is held at all. I expect a dispute here. Either way, the
   finding stands: depth-first, the endless alternative stops x = 1 from
   being taken up.
2. **P04a and P04b under absys and absys-wake-back.** These are classed
   *explicit* on x = 1, with *budget*. The other derivation, still
   elaborating `loop(x)`, denotes nothing under the least relation. I
   recorded it as an observation (SPECIFICATION, Outcomes 2: the more
   explicit valid form).
3. **P04d and P04f.** In every configuration the behaviour run is
   *error*: the kernel sent SIGKILL for lack of memory after about 3
   seconds. So nothing was reported, and the record cannot say whether
   every solution would eventually be reached.
4. **P06a and P06c, stage 1** are *unsound*. `not(x = 1)` is decided at
   once, at step 5. Its independent computation binds its own x to 1 and
   finds no contradiction, so the `not` fails, and no derivation survives.
   So decisions.md rules 18 and 19 ("waits") do not make this negation
   wait: it is negation as failure without a floundering check. P06a stage
   2 stays unsound. P06c stage 2 is *complete*, but only because the run
   had already failed.
5. **Empty reports.** I gave "no derivation survives" the representation
   *explicit*: the empty set of solutions, given as such. The
   specification has no class for this case, and others may use null.
6. **P07b residual** (`x + y = 10; 4 + y = x`). I flagged it as identical
   to the posed information, because the system only rewrote x − y = 4 in
   additive form and decided nothing. Someone could say *false*, on the
   grounds that it was rewritten.
7. **P08 under two readings.** `semantic` is a string ("open: …; closed:
   …"), with `semantic_open` and `semantic_closed` added as separate
   fields. At P08a stages 4 and 5, the unknowns are held as chains of
   suspended equations between unknowns, through auxiliary h₁…h₆. I
   classed that as *solved form* (identifications), checked equivalent by
   `check_p08a.py`, with the execution state *suspended*, as the harness
   gives it.
8. **Mode differences.** The only differences are in P04d and P04f, in
   every configuration. The cost and storage runs end in *timeout* (two
   attempts, 60 s and then 600 s). The behaviour run ended in *error*. The
   m2 reruns end in *error*, like the behaviour run. The semantic result
   is the same in all of them (none reported). Every other cost and
   storage stage matches its behaviour run.

## Rules I find ambiguous

- How to class the constants block: the brief does not say, and neither
  do METRICS or the harness README.
- When a held but untouched disjunct counts as "reported"
  (SPECIFICATION, Outcomes 2): the P04a depth-first case.
- The representation of an empty report.
- Whether a suspended equation between unknowns is still *suspended*
  work once the result is in solved form.
- Rule 5 (no anticipation) against a reformulation that names "cases
  still to come" (P08c).
- `batch-log.tsv` has interleaved and truncated lines around these runs,
  which looks like concurrent writes. I counted runs from the raw records
  instead: 90 behaviour records, matching every program and configuration.

## Files read outside the list

- No forbidden file was opened. Two listings went wider than the brief
  needed. `find systems/absys harnesses -maxdepth 3` listed file and
  directory *names* in `harnesses/python`, `harnesses/algol-60` and
  `harnesses/swi-prolog`, and `ls` of the repo root showed the names of
  `calibration/`, `reviews/`, `variants/` and `transcripts/`. I read no
  content in any of them.
- One long command output (the harness README and S-mechanisms.md) was
  saved by my tool environment to a file under
  `~/.claude/projects/…/tool-results/`, and I read it back there. Its
  content is only those two allowed files.
- My environment also put the user's auto-memory index (`~/.claude/…/memory/MEMORY.md`,
  two one-line entries unrelated to classing) into my context without my
  reading it. I did not use it.
- Several program headers cite `programs/absys/README.md` (the author's
  notes). I did not open it, nor `results/absys/RERUN-M2.md`, nor
  `results/absys/classes/`.

## Summary

**Tokens** (classifier A): 1436 tokens in 30 texts. **P 1421, R 15** (all
in P08c.ab1: the revmore alternative and revmore's definition head and
end), **C 0, S 0, H 0**. Each text is classed once, for all three
configurations.

**Outcomes**: 138 stage classifications, 46 per configuration.
- **Execution states:** 87 finished, 39 suspended, 6 budget (P04a and P04b
  in each configuration), 6 error (P04d and P04f).
- **Complete:** 72 (outside P08), including P04a, b, c and e; P06b, P06d,
  the P06e queries and P06c stage 2; and all of P07.
- **Unsound:** 9 (P06a stages 1 and 2, and P06c stage 1, in each
  configuration).
- **None reported:** 6 (P04d and P04f).
- **P08:**
  - P08a and P08b: complete under the open reading at every stage. Under
    the closed reading, unsound at stages 2–3 and complete from stage 4.
  - P08c primary: likewise (complete open; unsound closed at stages 2–3).
  - P08c.redefine: unsound open from stage 3, and unsound under both
    readings at stage 4.
- **Residuals in P07:** b and g reducible, c reduced, f inconsistency
  undetected; P07e's inconsistency is detected.

**Mode differences**: P04d and P04f cost and storage runs end in *timeout*
where the behaviour run is *error*, in all three configurations; the m2
reruns agree with the behaviour run (*error*).

**Expressibility**: P08c is *expressible with reformulation* (revmore);
every other sub-problem is *expressible*, in all three configurations.

**Late definition**: every P08 program is *code awaited*. P08c.redefine
is held only until the first, partial definition arrives, and then fails.

**S mechanisms**: none, in any program or configuration.
